# phyr

# What’s new in phyr 1.5.0

phyr 1.5.0 is a major update of
[`pglmm()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm.md), and
adds
[`phylo_signal()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/phylo_signal.md):

- **Large phylogenies.** Models are fitted with the sparse precision
  matrix of the phylogeny (`sparse = TRUE`, the default when possible),
  so time and memory grow about linearly with the number of species. A
  binomial model with 5000 species at 20 sites (80,000 observations) is
  fitted in about 5 seconds, versus about 11 minutes for `glmmTMB()`,
  with the same estimates
  ([benchmarks](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/articles/benchmarks.html)).
- **Laplace approximation by default.** Binomial and poisson models are
  fitted with the Laplace approximation instead of PQL, with the same
  estimates and log-likelihood as
  [`lme4::glmer()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lme4/man/glmer.html) and
  `glmmTMB()`.
- **More families.** Negative binomial (`"nbinomial"`) for overdispersed
  counts and `"Gamma"` for positive continuous responses, and
  [`offset()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/offset.html) terms in the
  formula.
- **Inference.** Profile likelihood confidence intervals of the
  variances ([`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html)),
  likelihood ratio tests of nested models
  ([`anova()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/anova.html)), and a full profile
  likelihood ratio test of each random term
  ([`pglmm_profile_LRT()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-profile-LRT.md)).
- **Standard model methods.**
  [`VarCorr()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/VarCorr.md),
  [`ranef()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/ranef.md) (one
  estimate per level, as lme4),
  [`fixef()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/fixef.md),
  [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html),
  [`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html),
  [`logLik()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/logLik.html)/[`AIC()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/AIC.html)/[`BIC()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/AIC.html),
  [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) with `newdata`,
  [`simulate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/simulate.html) (residual
  diagnostics with DHARMa),
  [`update()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/update.html), and
  [`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html)/[`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html)
  for broom.mixed and
  [`mice::pool()`](https://amices.org/mice/reference/pool.html), e.g. to
  combine fits with several candidate phylogenies.
- **Bayesian models with large phylogenies.** `bayes = TRUE` also uses
  the sparse precision matrix, either as a latent field over all nodes
  of the phylogeny (giving the posterior of ancestral states) or as a
  phylogenetic flow (giving the posterior of the rate of each branch).
- **Phylogenetic signal.**
  [`phylo_signal()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/phylo_signal.md)
  estimates Pagel’s lambda and Blomberg’s K, optionally with known
  standard errors of the species means, in time linear in the number of
  species: with 1000 species and measurement error, lambda takes 0.03
  seconds instead of about 2 minutes with
  [`phytools::phylosig()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/phytools/man/phylosig.html),
  and it reaches the maximum likelihood where other packages can stop
  short
  ([benchmarks](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/articles/benchmarks.html)).
  The trait can be a column of a data frame.

Some defaults and outputs changed
(e.g. [`ranef()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/ranef.md)
now returns per-level estimates; the variances are in
[`VarCorr()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/VarCorr.md)).
See the [NEWS](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/news/index.html) for the
breaking changes, and the vignette [“Usage of
pglmm()”](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/articles/pglmm.html) for
examples.

# Installation

To install the released version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("phyr")
```

To install the development version:

``` r

options(repos = c(
  phyr = 'https://daijiang.r-universe.dev',
  CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))
install.packages('phyr')

# or
remotes::install_github("daijiang/phyr")
```

# Main functions

The phyr package has four groups of functions:

1.  community phylogenetic diversity metrics (alpha: `psv`, `psr`,
    `pse`, etc. and beta: `pcd`), which were included in the `picante`
    package originally. They were updated with C++ to improve speed.
2.  models to estimate correlation between functional traits while
    accounting for phylogenetic relationships (`cor_phylo`), which was
    included in the `ape` package originally. It has new syntax, much
    improved performance (C++), and bootstrapping option.
3.  phylogenetic generalized linear mixed models (`pglmm`), which was
    originally included in the `pez` package. It has a model formula
    syntax similar to that of `lme4`, maximum likelihood fits with
    sparse matrices that scale to tens of thousands of species, and a
    Bayesian model fitting framework based on INLA.
    - Gaussian, binomial, poisson, negative binomial (`"nbinomial"`) and
      Gamma families; binomial and poisson models are fitted with the
      Laplace approximation by default, with the same estimates as
      [`lme4::glmer()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lme4/man/glmer.html) and
      `glmmTMB()`.
    - Confidence intervals
      ([`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html)), model
      comparison ([`anova()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/anova.html),
      [`pglmm_profile_LRT()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-profile-LRT.md)),
      predictions ([`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html),
      also for new data), simulations
      ([`simulate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/simulate.html), e.g. for
      residual diagnostics with DHARMa), and the methods of the broom
      packages
      ([`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html),
      [`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html)).
    - PGLMM for comparative data
      ([`pglmm_compare()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm_compare.md)),
      which was originally from
      [`ape::binaryPGLMM()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/ape/man/binaryPGLMM.html)
      but has more features.
    - We hope the model formula proposed here can be used to standardize
      PGLMMs set up across different tools (e.g. `brms` for Stan).
4.  phylogenetic signal of a trait (`phylo_signal`): Pagel’s lambda and
    Blomberg’s K, optionally with known standard errors of the species
    means (as
    [`phytools::phylosig()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/phytools/man/phylosig.html)),
    computed in time linear in the number of species.

# Usage examples of `pglmm()`

`pglmm` use similar syntax as
[`lme4::lmer`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lme4/man/lmer.html) to specify random
terms: add `__` (two underscores) at the end of grouping variable
(e.g. `sp`) to specify both phylogenetic and non-phylogenetic random
terms; use `(1|sp__@site)` to specify nested term (i.e. species
phylogenetic matrix `V_sp` nested within the diagonal of site matrix
`I_site`) to test phylogenetic overdispersion or underdispersion. This
should be the most commonly used one and is equal to
`kronecker(I_site, V_sp)`.

We can also use a second phylogeny for bipartite questions. For example,
`(1|parasite@host__)` will be converted to
`kronecker(V_host, I_parasite)`; `(1|parasite__@host__)` will be
converted to `kronecker(V_host, V_parasite)`.

For details about model formula, see documentation
[`?phyr::pglmm`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm.md) and
the vignette “Usage of pglmm()”. More application examples can be found
in [Ives 2018 Chapter 4](https://leanpub.com/correlateddata).

``` r

library(phyr)
```

``` r

# community data: abundance of each species at each site, with environmental
# variables of the sites
dat <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(comm_a), times = ncol(comm_a)),
  sp = rep(colnames(comm_a), each = nrow(comm_a)),
  freq = unlist(comm_a, use.names = FALSE)
)
dat <- merge(dat, envi, by = "site")
dat$pa <- as.numeric(dat$freq > 0)
head(dat)
##    site                   sp freq  sand shade   precip      tmin pa
## 1 s3293          Acer_rubrum    0 80.75  20.9 1.902397 0.1288019  0
## 2 s3293    Betula_papyrifera    0 80.75  20.9 1.902397 0.1288019  0
## 3 s3293 Achillea_millefolium    0 80.75  20.9 1.902397 0.1288019  0
## 4 s3293 Chimaphila_umbellata    0 80.75  20.9 1.902397 0.1288019  0
## 5 s3293      Amelanchier_spp    0 80.75  20.9 1.902397 0.1288019  0
## 6 s3293  Andropogon_gerardii    0 80.75  20.9 1.902397 0.1288019  0
# the phylogeny of the species in the data
phy <- ape::keep.tip(phylotree, unique(dat$sp))
# phy-LMM
test1 <- pglmm(freq ~ 1 + shade + (1|sp__) + (1|site) + (1|sp__@site),
               data = dat, family = "gaussian", REML = FALSE,
               cov_ranef = list(sp = phy))
test1
## Linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood
## 
## Formula: freq ~ 1 + shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site) + (1 | sp__@site)
## 
## logLik    AIC    BIC 
## -463.3  940.6  964.6 
## 
## Random effects:
##             Variance Std.Dev
## 1|sp          0.7389  0.8596
## 1|sp__        0.0000  0.0000
## 1|site        0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp__@site   0.0000  0.0000
## residual      3.2601  1.8056
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                  Value  Std.Error  Zscore    Pvalue    
## (Intercept) -0.1910424  0.3923414 -0.4869 0.6263086    
## shade        0.0226918  0.0067252  3.3741 0.0007405 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# confidence intervals: Wald for the fixed effects, profile likelihood for the variances
confint(test1)
##                    2.5 %     97.5 %
## (Intercept) -0.960017447 0.57793260
## shade        0.009510629 0.03587298
## 1|sp         0.000000000 1.93744853
## 1|sp__       0.000000000 1.79350790
## 1|site       0.000000000 0.20698144
## 1|sp__@site  0.000000000 0.47365994
## residual     2.542157590 3.97221767
# phy-GLMM (Laplace approximation)
test2 <- pglmm(pa ~ 1 + shade + (1|sp__) + (1|site) + (1|sp__@site),
               data = dat, family = "binomial", REML = FALSE,
               cov_ranef = list(sp = phy))
test2
## Generalized linear mixed model for binomial data fit by Laplace approximation (maximum likelihood)
## 
## Formula: pa ~ 1 + shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site) + (1 | sp__@site)
## 
## logLik    AIC    BIC 
## -123.3  258.5  279.0 
## 
## Random effects:
##             Variance Std.Dev
## 1|sp          0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp__        0.5094  0.7137
## 1|site        0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp__@site   0.0000  0.0000
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                  Value  Std.Error  Zscore    Pvalue    
## (Intercept) -2.2018863  0.6138136 -3.5872 0.0003342 ***
## shade        0.0173478  0.0089481  1.9387 0.0525361 .  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# is the phylogenetic nested term needed? likelihood ratio test
test2a <- pglmm(pa ~ 1 + shade + (1|sp__) + (1|site),
                data = dat, family = "binomial", REML = FALSE,
                cov_ranef = list(sp = phy))
anova(test2a, test2)
## test2a: pa ~ 1 + shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site)
## test2: pa ~ 1 + shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site) + (1 | sp__@site)
## 
##        npar    AIC    BIC  logLik deviance Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
## test2a    5 256.51 273.59 -123.25   246.51                    
## test2     6 258.51 279.00 -123.25   246.51     0  1          1
# bipartite
set.seed(42)
tree_site <- ape::rtree(n = length(unique(dat$site)), tip.label = sort(unique(dat$site)))
z_bipartite <- pglmm(freq ~ 1 + shade + (1|sp__) + (1|site__) +
                       (1|sp__@site) + (1|sp@site__) + (1|sp__@site__),
                     data = dat, family = "gaussian", REML = TRUE,
                     cov_ranef = list(sp = phy, site = tree_site))
z_bipartite
## Linear mixed model fit by restricted maximum likelihood
## 
## Formula: freq ~ 1 + shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site__) + (1 | sp__@site) + (1 | sp@site__) + (1 | sp__@site__)
## 
## logLik    AIC    BIC 
## -467.4  954.8  989.0 
## 
## Random effects:
##               Variance Std.Dev
## 1|sp            0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp__          0.7748  0.8802
## 1|site          0.0000  0.0000
## 1|site__        0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp__@site     0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp@site__     0.0000  0.0000
## 1|sp__@site__   0.0000  0.0000
## residual        3.2656  1.8071
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                  Value  Std.Error  Zscore    Pvalue    
## (Intercept) -0.2721731  0.5674007 -0.4797 0.6314521    
## shade        0.0226918  0.0067309  3.3713 0.0007482 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```

# Large phylogenies

With phylogenies in `cov_ranef`,
[`pglmm()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm.md) uses the
sparse precision matrix of the phylogeny (`sparse = TRUE`, the default
when possible), so that time and memory grow about linearly with the
number of species. For example, binomial and poisson models with 5000
species at 20 sites (80,000 observations) are fitted by maximum
likelihood in about 5 seconds, with the same estimates as `glmmTMB()`,
which needs about 11 minutes for these models:

``` r

nsp <- 5000
phy <- ape::rcoal(nsp, tip.label = paste0("sp", 1:nsp))
d <- expand.grid(sp = phy$tip.label, site = paste0("s", 1:20))
d$x <- rnorm(nrow(d))
d$y <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(0.3 * d$x))
fit <- pglmm(y ~ x + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site), data = d, family = "binomial",
             cov_ranef = list(sp = phy), REML = FALSE)
```

# Package index

## Phylogenetic Diversity

Functions to calculate alpha and beta phylogenetic diversity

- [`psv()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/psd.md)
  [`psr()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/psd.md)
  [`pse()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/psd.md)
  [`psc()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/psd.md)
  [`psv.spp()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/psd.md)
  [`psd()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/psd.md) :
  Phylogenetic Species Diversity Metrics
- [`pcd()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pcd.md) : pairwise
  site phylogenetic community dissimilarity (PCD) within a community
- [`pcd_pred()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pcd_pred.md)
  : Predicted PCD with species pool

## Phylogenetic Correlations

Functions to calculate correlations while accounting for phylogenetic
relationships.

- [`cor_phylo()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/cor_phylo.md)
  [`boot_ci(`*`<cor_phylo>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/cor_phylo.md)
  [`print(`*`<cor_phylo>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/cor_phylo.md)
  : Correlations among multiple variates with phylogenetic signal

- [`boot_ci()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/boot_ci.md) :
  Generic method to output bootstrap confidence intervals from an
  object.

- [`refit_boots()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/refit_boots.md)
  [`print(`*`<cp_refits>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/refit_boots.md)
  :

  Refit bootstrap replicates that failed to converge in a call to
  `cor_phylo`

## Phylogenetic Generalized Linear Mixed Models

Functions to fit PGLMMs.

- [`pglmm_matrix_structure()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-matrix-structure.md)
  [`communityPGLMM.matrix.structure()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-matrix-structure.md)
  :

  `pglmm_matrix_structure` produces the entire covariance matrix
  structure (V) when you specify random effects.

- [`pglmm_plot_ranef()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-plot-re.md)
  [`communityPGLMM.show.re()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-plot-re.md)
  [`pglmm_plot_re()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-plot-re.md)
  [`communityPGLMM.plot.re()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-plot-re.md)
  : Visualize random terms of communityPGLMMs

- [`pglmm_predicted_values()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-predicted-values.md)
  [`communityPGLMM.predicted.values()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-predicted-values.md)
  : Predicted values of PGLMM

- [`pglmm_profile_LRT()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-profile-LRT.md)
  [`communityPGLMM.profile.LRT()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-profile-LRT.md)
  : Testing statistical significance of random effect

- [`pglmm()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm.md)
  [`communityPGLMM()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm.md)
  : Phylogenetic Generalized Linear Mixed Model for Community Data

- [`pglmm_compare()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm_compare.md)
  [`predict(`*`<pglmm_compare>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm_compare.md)
  : Phylogenetic Generalized Linear Mixed Model for Comparative Data

- [`pglmm_iV()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm_iV.md)
  : Inverse of the covariance matrix of a fitted PGLMM

- [`prep_dat_pglmm()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/prep_dat_pglmm.md)
  :

  Prepare data for `pglmm`

- [`print(`*`<pglmm_compare>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/print.pglmm_compare.md)
  : Print summary information of fitted model

- [`ranef(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/ranef.md)
  [`print(`*`<ranef.pglmm>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/ranef.md)
  : Extract group-level estimates of random effects

- [`summary(`*`<pglmm_compare>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/summary.pglmm_compare.md)
  : Summary information of fitted pglmm_compare model

- [`VarCorr(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/VarCorr.md)
  : Extract variances of random terms

- [`anova(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/anova.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Likelihood ratio tests of nested models

- [`coef(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/coef.communityPGLMM.md)
  [`df.residual(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/coef.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Fixed effects of a fitted pglmm

- [`confint(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/confint.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Confidence intervals for the parameters of a fitted pglmm

- [`family(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/family.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Family Objects for communityPGLMM objects

- [`fitted(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/fitted.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Fitted values for communityPGLMM

- [`fixef(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/fixef.md)
  : Extract fixed-effects estimates

- [`formula(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/formula.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Formula of a fitted pglmm

- [`logLik(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/logLik.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Log-likelihood of a communityPGLMM Model

- [`model.frame(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/model.frame.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Extracting the Model Frame from a communityPGLMM Model object

- [`nobs(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/nobs.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Number of Observation in a communityPGLMM Model

- [`plot_data()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-plot-data.md)
  [`plot_bayes(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/pglmm-plot-data.md)
  : Plot the original dataset and predicted values (optional)

- [`predict(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/predict.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Predict Function for communityPGLMM Model Objects

- [`print(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/print.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Print summary information of fitted model

- [`residuals(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/residuals.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Residuals of communityPGLMM objects

- [`simulate(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/simulate.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Simulate from a communityPGLMM object

- [`summary(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/summary.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Summary information of fitted model

- [`tidy(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/tidy.communityPGLMM.md)
  [`glance(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/tidy.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Tidy and glance methods for pglmm fits

- [`vcov(`*`<communityPGLMM>`*`)`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/vcov.communityPGLMM.md)
  : Covariance matrix of the fixed effects

- [`get_design_matrix()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/get_design_matrix_pglmm.md)
  :

  `get_design_matrix` gets design matrix for gaussian, binomial, and
  poisson models

- [`plot_bayes()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/plot_bayes.md)
  : plot_bayes generic

## Phylogenetic Signal

Pagel’s lambda and Blomberg’s K, with known measurement error, in linear
time.

- [`phylo_signal()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/phylo_signal.md)
  : Phylogenetic signal with known measurement error

## Helper Functions

Functions to help with data processing.

- [`vcv2()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/vcv2.md) : Create
  phylogenetic var-cov matrix
- [`rm_site_noobs()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/rm_site_noobs.md)
  : Remove site that has no observations of any species
- [`rm_sp_noobs()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/rm_sp_noobs.md)
  : Remove species that not observed in any site
- [`` `%nin%` ``](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/nin.md) :
  Not in
- [`align_comm_V()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/align_comm_V.md)
  : Create phylogenetic var-cov matrix based on phylogeny and community
  data
- [`match_comm_tree()`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/match_comm_tree.md)
  : Match phylogeny with community data

## Data Sets

Examplary data sets used in the package

- [`comm_a`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/comm_a.md) :
  Example community data
- [`comm_b`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/comm_b.md) :
  Example community data
- [`traits`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/traits.md) :
  Example species traits data
- [`phylotree`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/phylotree.md)
  : Example phylogeny
- [`envi`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/envi.md) : Example
  environmental data
- [`oldfield`](https://daijiang.github.io/phyr/reference/oldfield.md) :
  Phylogeny and community data from an Oldfield ecosystem in Southern
  Ontario, Canada
